Based on my analysis of the full diff and commit history, here is the squash commit message for the feature's final state:

feat(CC-0114): seed K-ORC bootstrap clouds.yaml from operator

- Add seedBootstrapCloudsYAML to the c5c3-operator's reconcileKORC: it
  write-if-empty seeds a password-based clouds.yaml into the
  {name}-admin-app-credential Secret so K-ORC's admin imports can
  authenticate before the application credential is minted, breaking the
  AdminCredentialReady chicken-and-egg deadlock on a fresh cluster
  without any external shell seed
- Make the seed never clobber a minted credential-based clouds.yaml;
  after a re-mint deletes the key, the next pass re-seeds the password
  document to bridge the re-authentication gap, and the generated
  "value" key is never touched
- Add ensureKORCCloudsYAMLExternalSecret: the operator now creates and
  owns a per-ControlPlane ExternalSecret in the child namespace
  (controller owner-ref'd for GC) reading the per-CR OpenBao path, so an
  arbitrarily named ControlPlane resolves to the correct key with no
  manifest edit
- Wire the seed -> admin app-cred PushSecret -> ExternalSecret steps
  into reconcileKORC ahead of the AC mint, each with a dedicated
  KORCReady failure reason (SeedCloudsYamlError, PushSecretError,
  ExternalSecretError)
- Reduce deploy/eso/externalsecrets/k-orc-clouds-yaml.yaml to only the
  orc-system global-default copy; the control-plane-namespace
  ExternalSecret is now operator-created per-CR
- Remove seed_korc_bootstrap_clouds_yaml from write-bootstrap-secrets.sh
  so the shell bootstrap seeds only the per-CR Model B admin password and
  no longer marks the app-credential path ESO-managed
- Drop the KORC_KEYSTONE_AUTH_URL override from deploy-infra.sh; the
  operator derives the in-cluster Keystone auth_url per-CR from the
  ControlPlane name, so the CR name is no longer pinned by a pre-seeded
  clouds.yaml
- Replace the old fresh-cluster deadlock unit test with tests asserting
  reconcileKORC seeds the password clouds.yaml and creates both the
  backup PushSecret and the per-CR ExternalSecret
- Add unit tests for seedBootstrapCloudsYAML (write-if-empty,
  no-overwrite-minted, repopulate-after-remint, rendered document parses
  with internal endpoint_type and the projected per-CR auth_url)
- Add unit tests for ensureKORCCloudsYAMLExternalSecret (shape and owner
  ref, per-CR remote key for a non-default name, idempotent no-churn) and
  reconcileKORC edge cases (defers before seeding when the admin password
  is missing; steady-state pass does not churn a minted clouds.yaml)
- Update the envtest integration test to assert the operator-created
  ExternalSecret's shape and ControlPlane owner ref instead of
  pre-creating it
- Extend the multi-controlplane E2E chainsaw test to assert each tenant's
  per-CR ExternalSecret is operator-owned with the correct per-CR
  remoteRef.key, add a wait_ready_condition helper, and raise the timeout
  budget for the two new ExternalSecret waits
- Refresh the quick-start, ControlPlane CRD reference, reconciler
  reference, and infrastructure-manifests docs to describe the
  operator-owned bootstrap seed and per-CR ExternalSecret
